newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2943 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2950 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based China national interbank foreign exchange market.
But the close was sharply down against Wednesday's weighted average price of 8.2916.
Dealers said the yuan moved downward for most of the Thursday session due to selling by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, and some follow-up offers.
The yuan opened higher at an intraday high of 8.2917 and remained stable in early trading around the opening price.
It then consolidated down for the rest of the session, hitting a low of 8.2950 in late trading.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2925, traders said.
One dealer said market sentiment was hurt by the central bank's persistent efforts to depress the yuan, and was the reason the currency fell for most of the session.
"The People's Bank of China managed to depress the yuan late in trading in the past two days," he said.
"The intervention weakened sentiment and led to today's downward spiral," he said.

Another reason for the downward trend was light demand for the local currency right after the Chinese lunar new year holiday, which closed the market from last Friday until Wednesday this week, traders said.
Dealers expected the yuan to consolidate down on Friday.
The yuan closed up slightly at 6.6700 from 6.6768 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0706 from 1.0709 against the Hong Kong dollar.
